The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Story With a Hole in It

“Once there was a very grand pea,” began Caty. She was trying out a tale for Everybody Day. “It rolled all the way to the edge of the world. And then it… it…”

The next bit had gone clean out of her head. Toad hunted under the stump in case it had fallen there. Bella lifted Caty’s tail. “Nothing here,” she reported.

Caty felt hot under her cheek feathers. She was supposed to be telling the story. “I think I’ve made a hole in it,” she whispered. From the edge of the crowd Moth whispered, “How big?”

“Pea-sized, I suppose.” Moth thought for a while. “Big enough for a boat, then. My pea would set sail in its own pod.” Caty could see it! Two curly ends. A stem for a mast.

Caty tried the story again. When the pea reached the edge of the world, she cupped her wings around an empty place. Moth sailed her boat right into the quiet.

“What did the pea pack?” Caty asked. “A smaller pea,” said Toad. “What did that pea pack?” asked Bella. Toad opened his mouth. He closed it. He could see where this was going.

They sailed that pea all the way to supper. Caty drew a curling story line on a leaf for the Welcome Tree. She left the end open. Moth asked to tell the first bit next time.

At supper, a pea rolled off Caty’s plate. Four birds watched it roll. It came to rest by a spoon. “Well?” Bella asked. Caty settled back to listen.
